status.en: 15 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 88% more than the week before, most of them in Kivu, Kinshasa and Kigali.
status.nb: 15 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 88 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Kivu, Kinshasa og Kigali.

summary.en: M23 rebels continue offensive in eastern DRC, seizing towns and planning 3,300 houses to ease the Goma housing crisis, while ADF gunmen keep killing civilians in Ituri province. The FARDC was blamed for bombing a school in Minembwe, leaving 738 students without classes. Rwanda is preparing to serve as a European deportation hub for asylum seekers, prompting diplomatic protest from the DRC. The Kinshasa blind spot analysis notes that Kenya-DRC détente requires broader regional cooperation. 1,158 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: M23‑opprørerne fortsetter offensiven i østlige DRC, erobrer byer og planlegger 3 300 hus for å lindre boligmangelen i Goma, mens ADF-våpnede fortsetter å drepe sivile i Ituri-provinsen. FARDC ble anklaget for å ha bombet en skole i Minembwe, noe som etterlot 738 elever uten undervisning. Rwanda forbereder seg på å fungere som et europeisk deportasjonssenter for asylsøkere, noe som har ført til diplomatisk protest fra DRC. Kinshasa-blindspott-analysen påpeker at Kenya-DRC-détente krever bredere regionalt samarbeid. 1 158 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: M23 campaign (2022–present)
background.extract: The M23 campaign is an ongoing series of military offensives launched by the March 23 Movement (M23), a Rwandan-backed rebel paramilitary group in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, since March 2022. In November 2021, M23 first launched attacks against the Congolese military (FARDC) and MONUSCO, seizing military positions in Ndiza, Cyanzu, and Runyoni in North Kivu Province. This coincided with the deployment of Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) to the region to combat the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan rebel group operating in the Congo's North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
